title: How do you draw and label an angle with arms ST and SR?
description: An angle is drawn from the names of its two arms. The common letter gives the vertex, the two rays are drawn from it, a small curve is marked at the vertex, and the angle is named with the vertex in the middle.
teaching_notes: One idea: when two arms are named, the letter they share is the vertex, and both rays start there. Watch for students who draw the rays from T or from R, or who write the vertex at the end of the name.

source: Draw and label an angle with arms ST and SR.
video_script.why: The child reads the shared letter of the two arms as the vertex, draws both rays from it, and names the angle with the vertex in the middle.
video_script.substitution: Draw the rays ST and SR from the shared point S, and mark a small curve between them.
video_script.anchor: an empty page, with the arms named ST and SR
video_script.payoff_line: The vertex is S, and the angle is R S T

final_answer.value: Draw the rays ST and SR from S, with a small curve at S. The vertex is S and the angle is angle RST, or angle TSR
final_answer.spoken: draw the rays S T and S R from S, with a small curve at S. The vertex is S, and the angle is R S T, or T S R

never_show: the name of the angle, before the answer beat
maths_rules: The two arms ST and SR both start at S, so S is the common starting point.
The common starting point of the two arms is the vertex, so the vertex is S.
Ray ST starts at S and passes through T, and ray SR starts at S and passes through R.
A small curve is marked at the vertex, between the two arms.
The vertex is the middle letter in the name, so the angle is RST, or TSR.
video_script.design: One idea: the letter shared by the two arms is the vertex, and both rays start from it. A blank page gets the point S, then the two rays, then the curve. The method is the same way as the examples in the book on the arms and the vertex of an angle.
